subject: maths
title: Primary 5 Fractions and Division
seo_title: P5 Fractions and Division Worksheets: Free Primary 5 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Dividing a whole number by a whole number with quotient as a fraction; expressing fractions as decimals
meta_desc: Free P5 maths practice: 3 ÷ 4 = 3/4, 7 ÷ 3 = 2 1/3, fractions as decimals, rounding to 2 decimal places and bar model problems. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
A division is a fraction

When a whole number is divided by a whole number, the answer can be a fraction. The number being divided is the numerator. The number we divide by is the denominator.

3 ÷ 4 = 34

Answers greater than 1

If the number being divided is bigger, the answer is more than 1. Write it as a mixed number. The remainder is shared too, so it goes over the number we divide by.

Example

7 ÷ 3 = ?

7 ÷ 3 = 2 remainder 1. The 1 left over is shared among 3, so it is 13. 7 ÷ 3 = 73 = 2 13.

Answer: 2 13

Fractions as decimals

If the denominator goes into 10 or 100, make an equivalent fraction. Otherwise, divide the numerator by the denominator.

Example

Write 920 as a decimal.

20 × 5 = 100, so multiply the top by 5 too: 920 = 45100.

Answer: 0.45

Correct to 2 decimal places

Some divisions never end. Divide to 3 decimal places, then look at the 3rd digit. If it is 5 or more, round up. If it is less than 5, round down.

Word problems with a model

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
3 ÷ 4 = 43The number being divided goes on top: 3 ÷ 4 = 34
7 ÷ 3 = 2 r 1 = 2.1The remainder is shared too: 2 13 ≈ 2.33
7 ÷ 3 = 2 17Put the remainder over 3, the number you divide by
18 = 0.8Divide: 1 ÷ 8 = 0.125
23 = 0.66 (2 d.p.)Look at the 3rd place: 0.666… rounds up to 0.67

faq.q: What is taught in P5 fractions and division?
faq.a: Primary 5 students learn that dividing one whole number by another gives a fraction, such as 3 ÷ 4 = 3/4 and 7 ÷ 3 = 2 1/3. They also write fractions as decimals, such as 3/8 = 0.375, and give answers correct to 2 decimal places.

faq.q: How do I explain 3 ÷ 4 = 3/4 to my child?
faq.a: Share 3 pizzas among 4 people: cut every pizza into quarters and give each person 1 quarter of each pizza, so each person gets 3 quarters. Drawing the pizzas or a bar model makes the idea easy to see.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake in fractions and division?
faq.a: Writing the remainder as a decimal, such as 7 ÷ 3 = 2.1. The remainder 1 is shared among 3 too, so 7 ÷ 3 = 2 1/3, which is about 2.33. Turning the fraction upside down (3 ÷ 4 = 4/3) is the other common slip.

faq.q: Is fractions and division in the MOE Primary 5 syllabus?
faq.a: Yes. The 2021 MOE Primary Mathematics syllabus for Primary 5 includes dividing a whole number by a whole number with the quotient as a fraction, and expressing fractions as decimals. These skills are used again in Primary 6 and the PSLE.

items.q: 1 pizza is shared equally among 3 children. The shaded slice is one child’s share. How much pizza does each child get?
c: 23 of a pizza
13 of a pizza
items.e: 1 pizza cut into 3 equal slices: each child gets 1 slice = 13. So 1 ÷ 3 = 13. 0.3 is not 13: it is 310.

items.q: 3 pizzas are shared equally among 4 children. The shaded slices are one child’s share. How much pizza does each child get?
c: 13 of a pizza
14 of a pizza
34 of a pizza
43 of a pizza
items.e: Cut each pizza into 4 equal slices. Each child gets 1 slice from each of the 3 pizzas: 3 quarters = 34. So 3 ÷ 4 = 34, not 43.

items.q: 2 pizzas are shared equally among 3 children. How much pizza does each child get?
c: 23 of a pizza
32 of a pizza
25 of a pizza
13 of a pizza
items.e: Each pizza is cut into 3 equal slices. Each child gets 1 slice of each pizza: 2 thirds = 23. 2 ÷ 3 = 23. 13 counts the slices of only one pizza.

items.q: 2 cakes are shared equally among 5 friends. The shaded parts are one friend’s share. How much cake does each friend get?
c: 52 of a cake
27 of a cake
15 of a cake
25 of a cake
items.e: Cut each cake into 5 equal parts. Each friend gets 1 part of each of the 2 cakes: 2 fifths = 25. Do not add 2 and 5: the denominator is the number of friends.

items.q: 4 cakes are shared equally among 5 friends. How much cake does each friend get?
c: 14 of a cake
45 of a cake
15 of a cake
54 of a cake
items.e: Each friend gets 1 fifth of each of the 4 cakes: 4 fifths. 4 ÷ 5 = 45. 54 is 5 ÷ 4, the wrong way round.
The number being divided goes on top: 3 ÷ 5 = 35. 53 is 5 ÷ 3.
5 ÷ 8 = 58. The 5 is divided, so it is the numerator. 38 comes from 8 − 5.
1 whole shared into 6 equal parts: each part is 16. 6 is 6 ÷ 1, and 0.16 just writes the digits.
7 ÷ 10 = 710 = 0.7. 0.07 is 7100.

items.q: Which division is the same as 59?
items.e: A fraction is a division: numerator ÷ denominator. 59 = 5 ÷ 9.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 4 ÷ 7?
items.e: 4 ÷ 7 = 47. Sharing 4 wholes among 7 gives each share 4 sevenths. 74 is 7 ÷ 4.
11 ÷ 12 = 1112. 11 is less than 12, so the answer is less than 1.

items.q: Find the missing number: 6 ÷ ? = 611
items.e: The denominator is the number we divide by: 6 ÷ 11 = 611.

items.q: Find the missing number: ? ÷ 9 = 49
items.e: The numerator is the number being divided: 4 ÷ 9 = 49. 36 is 4 × 9.

items.q: Which is not equal to 2 ÷ 3?
items.e: 2 ÷ 3 = 23 = 46, and 4 ÷ 6 = 46 = 23. 32 is 3 ÷ 2, which is more than 1.

items.q: 6 ÷ 8 = ? Give the answer in simplest form.
items.e: 6 ÷ 8 = 68. Divide the numerator and the denominator by 2: 34. 38 divides only the numerator.

items.q: 4 ÷ 10 = ? Give the answer in simplest form.
items.e: 4 ÷ 10 = 410. Divide the top and the bottom by 2: 25. 45 divides only the denominator.

items.q: 8 ÷ 12 = ? Give the answer in simplest form.
items.e: 8 ÷ 12 = 812. Divide the top and the bottom by 4: 23. Whatever you divide the numerator by, divide the denominator by the same number.

items.q: Which gives each person more: 2 cakes shared among 5 people, or 2 cakes shared among 3 people?
items.e: 2 ÷ 5 = 25 and 2 ÷ 3 = 23. Thirds are bigger than fifths, so 23 > 25. Fewer people means a bigger share: among 3 people.

items.q: Each child gets 38 of a pizza. Which sharing gives this?
items.e: 38 = 3 ÷ 8, so 3 pizzas are shared among 8 children. 8 pizzas among 3 children gives 83 each.

items.q: 5 pizzas are shared equally between 2 children. The shaded halves are one child’s share. How much pizza does each child get?
c: 12 of a pizza
25 of a pizza
items.e: Each child gets 1 half of each of the 5 pizzas: 5 halves = 52 = 2 12. 5 ÷ 2 = 2 remainder 1, and the 1 pizza left over is cut into halves. It is not 2.1.

items.q: 5 cakes are shared equally among 4 friends. How much cake does each friend get?
c: 45 of a cake
items.e: Each friend gets 1 quarter of each of the 5 cakes: 5 quarters = 54 = 1 14. 45 is 4 ÷ 5.

items.q: 7 ÷ 3 = ? Give the answer as a mixed number.
items.e: 7 ÷ 3 = 2 remainder 1. The remainder 1 is still shared among 3, so it is 13. 7 ÷ 3 = 73 = 2 13. The remainder is not the decimal .1.

items.q: 9 ÷ 2 = ? Give the answer as a mixed number.
items.e: 9 ÷ 2 = 4 remainder 1. The remainder 1 is still shared among 2, so it is 12. 9 ÷ 2 = 92 = 4 12. The remainder is not the decimal .1.

items.q: 13 ÷ 5 = ? Give the answer as a mixed number.
items.e: 13 ÷ 5 = 2 remainder 3. The remainder 3 is still shared among 5, so it is 35. 13 ÷ 5 = 135 = 2 35. The remainder is not the decimal .3.

items.q: Write 10 ÷ 3 as an improper fraction.
items.e: 10 ÷ 3 = 103 (= 3 13). 310 is 3 ÷ 10, and 3.1 writes the remainder as a decimal.

items.q: Each whole on the number line is split into 4 equal parts. The red dot shows 11 ÷ 4. What number is at the red dot?
items.e: Each part is 14. The dot is 11 parts from 0: 114. That is 2 wholes and 3 more parts = 2 34. 3 14 is 1 part after 3, but the dot is 1 part before 3.

items.q: 17 ÷ 6 = ? Give the answer as a mixed number.
items.e: 17 ÷ 6 = 2 remainder 5. The remainder 5 is still shared among 6, so it is 56. 17 ÷ 6 = 176 = 2 56. The remainder is not the decimal .5.

items.q: 23 ÷ 4 = ? Give the answer as a mixed number.
items.e: 23 ÷ 4 = 5 remainder 3. The remainder 3 is still shared among 4, so it is 34. 23 ÷ 4 = 234 = 5 34. The remainder is not the decimal .3.

items.q: 29 ÷ 5 = 5 remainder 4. Which mixed number is 29 ÷ 5?
items.e: The remainder 4 is shared among 5, so it is 45. 29 ÷ 5 = 5 45. Do not put the remainder over 29.

items.q: Between which two whole numbers is 19 ÷ 4?
items.e: 4 × 4 = 16 and 5 × 4 = 20, so 19 ÷ 4 = 4 34 is between 4 and 5.

items.q: Which division has the answer 3 25?
items.e: 3 25 = 3 wholes and 2 fifths. 3 × 5 + 2 = 17 fifths, so 3 25 = 175 = 17 ÷ 5.

items.q: Which division has the answer 4 13?
items.e: 4 × 3 + 1 = 13, so 4 13 = 133 = 13 ÷ 3. 12 ÷ 3 = 4 forgets the remainder.

items.q: Write 2 38 as a division of two whole numbers.
items.e: 2 × 8 + 3 = 19, so 2 38 = 198 = 19 ÷ 8. 23 ÷ 8 just joins the digits 2 and 3.

items.q: Find the missing number: ? ÷ 4 = 3 34
items.e: 3 34 = 3 wholes and 3 quarters. 3 × 4 + 3 = 15, so 15 ÷ 4 = 3 34. 12 ÷ 4 is only 3.

items.q: 15 ÷ 6 = ? Give the answer in simplest form.
items.e: 15 ÷ 6 = 2 remainder 3 = 2 36. Simplify: 36 = 12, so the answer is 2 12.

items.q: 14 ÷ 4 = ? Give the answer in simplest form.
items.e: 14 ÷ 4 = 3 remainder 2 = 3 24 = 3 12. 27 is 4 ÷ 14 in simplest form.

items.q: 26 ÷ 8 = ? Give the answer in simplest form.
items.e: 26 ÷ 8 = 3 remainder 2 = 3 28. Simplify: 28 = 14, so the answer is 3 14.

items.q: Which is greater: 9 ÷ 4 or 11 ÷ 5?
items.e: 9 ÷ 4 = 2 14 and 11 ÷ 5 = 2 15. Both have 2 wholes, and 14 > 15, so 9 ÷ 4 is greater.

items.q: Some cakes are shared equally among 3 children. Each child gets 1 23 cakes. How many cakes are there?
items.e: 1 23 = 53, and 53 × 3 = 153 = 5 cakes. Check: 5 ÷ 3 = 1 23. 3 23 multiplies only the whole number.

items.q: The shaded part is 14 of the hundred square. Write 14 as a decimal.
items.e: 25 of the 100 squares are shaded. 14 = 25100 = 0.25. 0.14 just writes the digits 1 and 4.

items.q: The shaded part is 35 of the hundred square. Write 35 as a decimal.
items.e: 60 of the 100 squares are shaded. 35 = 610 = 60100 = 0.6. 0.06 would be only 6 squares.

items.q: Write 12 as a decimal.
items.e: 12 = 510 = 0.5. (1 ÷ 2 = 0.5.) 0.12 just writes the digits.

items.q: Write 710 as a decimal.
items.e: 710 is 7 tenths = 0.7. 0.07 is 7 hundredths.

items.q: Write 37100 as a decimal.
items.e: 37100 is 37 hundredths. Hundredths are the second place after the decimal point: 0.37.

items.q: Write 25 as a decimal.
items.e: Make the denominator 10: 25 = 410 = 0.4. 2.5 is 5 ÷ 2, the wrong way round.

items.q: Write 34 as a decimal.
items.e: Make the denominator 100: 34 = 75100 = 0.75. 0.34 just writes the digits 3 and 4.

items.q: Write 920 as a decimal.
items.e: 20 × 5 = 100, so multiply the top by 5 too: 920 = 45100 = 0.45.

items.q: Write 625 as a decimal.
items.e: 25 × 4 = 100, so 625 = 24100 = 0.24. 0.625 just writes the digits.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.6?
items.e: 0.6 = 610 = 35 (divide the top and the bottom by 2). 6100 = 0.06.

items.q: Write 18 as a decimal.
items.e: 1 ÷ 8: 10 ÷ 8 = 1 r 2, 20 ÷ 8 = 2 r 4, 40 ÷ 8 = 5. So 18 = 0.125. 0.8 is 810, not 18.

items.q: The working shows 3 ÷ 8. What is 38 as a decimal?
items.e: 30 ÷ 8 = 3 r 6, 60 ÷ 8 = 7 r 4, 40 ÷ 8 = 5. So 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375. Keep dividing until nothing is left.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.08?
items.e: 0.08 = 8 hundredths = 8100 = 225 (divide by 4). 45 = 0.8.

items.q: 7 ÷ 4 = ? Give the answer as a decimal.
items.e: 7 ÷ 4 = 1 remainder 3. The 3 left over is 34 = 0.75. So 7 ÷ 4 = 1.75. 1.3 writes the remainder as a decimal.

items.q: 9 ÷ 5 = ? Give the answer as a decimal.
items.e: 9 ÷ 5 = 1 remainder 4, and 45 = 810 = 0.8. So 9 ÷ 5 = 1.8, not 1.4.

items.q: 3 ÷ 20 = ? Give the answer as a decimal.
items.e: 3 ÷ 20 = 320 = 15100 = 0.15. 6.67 is about 20 ÷ 3, the wrong way round.

items.q: Write 2 34 as a decimal.
items.e: The 2 wholes stay. 34 = 0.75, so 2 34 = 2.75.

items.q: Write 1 720 as a decimal.
items.e: 720 = 35100 = 0.35, so 1 720 = 1.35. 1.72 just writes the digits.

items.q: Write 138 as a decimal.
items.e: 13 ÷ 8 = 1 remainder 5, and 58 = 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625. So 138 = 1.625. 1.5 writes the remainder as a decimal.

items.q: Which is the greatest?
items.e: Change to decimals: 58 = 0.625, 35 = 0.6, 0.55 and 0.59. The greatest is 58.

sets.title: Fractions as decimals correct to 2 decimal places

items.q: Write 13 as a decimal correct to 2 decimal places.
items.e: 1 ÷ 3 = 0.333… The 3rd decimal place is 3, which is less than 5, so round down: 0.33. 0.3 has only 1 decimal place.

items.q: The working shows 2 ÷ 3 to 3 decimal places. What is 23 correct to 2 decimal places?
items.e: 2 ÷ 3 = 0.666… The 3rd decimal place is 6, which is 5 or more, so round up: 0.67. 0.66 cuts off the digits without rounding.

items.q: Write 16 as a decimal correct to 2 decimal places.
items.e: 1 ÷ 6 = 0.166… Look at the 3rd decimal place: 6 is 5 or more, so round up: 0.17. 0.16 forgets to round.

items.q: Write 17 as a decimal correct to 2 decimal places.
items.e: 1 ÷ 7 = 0.142… The 3rd decimal place is 2, which is less than 5, so round down: 0.14. 0.17 just writes the digits.

items.q: Write 57 as a decimal correct to 2 decimal places.
items.e: 5 ÷ 7 = 0.714… The 3rd decimal place is 4, which is less than 5, so round down: 0.71. 1.4 is 7 ÷ 5.

items.q: Write 56 as a decimal correct to 2 decimal places.
items.e: 5 ÷ 6 = 0.833… The 3rd decimal place is 3, so the 2nd place stays: 0.83. 1.2 is 6 ÷ 5, the wrong way round.

items.q: Write 49 as a decimal correct to 2 decimal places.
items.e: 4 ÷ 9 = 0.444… The 4s go on for ever. The 3rd decimal place is 4, so round down: 0.44.

items.q: Write 59 as a decimal correct to 2 decimal places.
items.e: 5 ÷ 9 = 0.555… The 5s go on for ever. The 3rd decimal place is 5, so round up: 0.56. 0.55 forgets to round.

items.q: Write 27 as a decimal correct to 2 decimal places.
items.e: 2 ÷ 7 = 0.285… The 3rd decimal place is 5, so round up: 0.29. 3.5 is 7 ÷ 2, the wrong way round.

items.q: Write 712 as a decimal correct to 2 decimal places.
items.e: 7 ÷ 12 = 0.583… The 3rd decimal place is 3, so round down: 0.58. 0.6 is correct to only 1 decimal place.

items.q: Write 38 as a decimal correct to 2 decimal places.
items.e: 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375. The 3rd decimal place is 5, so round up: 0.38. 0.4 is correct to only 1 decimal place.

items.q: Write 78 as a decimal correct to 2 decimal places.
items.e: 7 ÷ 8 = 0.875. The 3rd decimal place is 5, so round up: 0.88.

items.q: Write 116 as a decimal correct to 2 decimal places.
items.e: 1 ÷ 16 = 0.0625. The 3rd decimal place is 2, so round down: 0.06. 0.16 just writes the digits.

items.q: Siti wrote: 23 = 0.66 (correct to 2 decimal places). What did she do wrong?
items.e: 2 ÷ 3 = 0.666… The 3rd decimal place is 6, which is 5 or more, so the answer rounds up to 0.67. She did not round up.

items.q: Find the value of 10 ÷ 3 correct to 2 decimal places.
items.e: 10 ÷ 3 = 3.333… The remainder 1 is not .1: keep dividing. The 3rd decimal place is 3, so round down: 3.33.

items.q: Find the value of 17 ÷ 6 correct to 2 decimal places.
items.e: 17 ÷ 6 = 2.833… The 3rd decimal place is 3, so round down: 2.83. 2.5 writes the remainder 5 as a decimal.

items.q: Find the value of 25 ÷ 7 correct to 2 decimal places.
items.e: 25 ÷ 7 = 3.571… The 3rd decimal place is 1, so round down: 3.57. 3.4 writes the remainder 4 as a decimal, and 0.28 is 7 ÷ 25.

items.q: Write 2 59 as a decimal correct to 2 decimal places.
items.e: 23 ÷ 9 = 2.555… The 3rd decimal place is 5, so round up: 2.56. 2.59 just writes the digits.

items.q: Write 116 as a decimal correct to 2 decimal places.
items.e: 11 ÷ 6 = 1.833… The 3rd decimal place is 3, so round down: 1.83. 1.5 writes the remainder 5 as a decimal, and 0.55 is 6 ÷ 11.

items.q: Which fraction is 0.43 when written as a decimal correct to 2 decimal places?
items.e: 37 = 3 ÷ 7 = 0.428… ≈ 0.43. 49 ≈ 0.44, 25 = 0.4 and 43 ≈ 1.33.

items.q: Ali pours 3 ℓ of water equally into 4 bottles. How much water is in each bottle?
items.e: 3 ℓ shared among 4 bottles: 3 ÷ 4 = 34 ℓ. 43 ℓ would be 4 ℓ in 3 bottles.

items.q: Mdm Wong packs 2 kg of rice equally into 5 bags. How much rice is in each bag?
items.e: 2 ÷ 5 = 25 = 410 = 0.4 kg. 2.5 kg is 5 ÷ 2, the wrong way round.

items.q: Mrs Lim cuts a 9 m ribbon into 4 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
items.e: 4 units = 9 m, so 1 unit = 9 ÷ 4 = 94 m = 2 14 m. 9 ÷ 4 = 2 remainder 1, and the 1 m left over is cut into quarters, so it is not 2.1 m.

items.q: Hui Min runs 4 rounds of the school track and covers 3 km. How long is one round?
items.e: 3 ÷ 4 = 34 km = 0.75 km. 1.33 km is about 4 ÷ 3, the wrong way round.

items.q: A 2 ℓ bottle of soya bean milk is poured equally into 8 cups. How much milk is in each cup?
items.e: 2 ÷ 8 = 14 ℓ. 1 ℓ = 1000 ml, so 14 ℓ = 1000 ÷ 4 = 250 ml. 25 ml forgets that 1 ℓ is 1000 ml.

items.q: Mr Kumar paid $18 for 4 bowls of laksa. Each bowl cost the same. How much did one bowl cost?
items.e: 4 units = $18, so 1 unit = $18 ÷ 4 = $4 12 = $4.50. 18 ÷ 4 = 4 remainder 2, and the $2 left over is $0.50 for each bowl, not 20¢.

items.q: 8 pizzas are shared equally among 6 children. How much pizza does each child get?
c: 34 of a pizza
items.e: 8 ÷ 6 = 1 remainder 2 = 1 26 = 1 13. Put the remainder over 6, the number of children, not over 8.

items.q: A baker uses 7 kg of flour for 8 equal batches of curry puffs. How much flour is in each batch?
items.e: 7 ÷ 8 = 78 kg (= 0.875 kg). 1 17 kg is 8 ÷ 7, the wrong way round.

items.q: 7 durians are shared equally among 4 families. How many durians does each family get?
items.e: 7 ÷ 4 = 1 remainder 3 = 1 34 durians. The 3 left over are shared among 4 families, so 34 each.

items.q: Farah cuts 3 m of cloth into 8 equal pieces. How long is each piece in centimetres?
items.e: 3 ÷ 8 = 38 m = 0.375 m. 1 m = 100 cm, so 0.375 m = 37.5 cm.

items.q: Sarah’s mother divides 3 kg of prawns equally into 4 bags. How many grams of prawns are in each bag?
items.e: 3 ÷ 4 = 34 kg = 0.75 kg. 1 kg = 1000 g, so 0.75 kg = 750 g. 250 g is only 14 kg.

items.q: 8 friends share the cost of a $50 birthday cake equally. How much does each friend pay?
items.e: $50 ÷ 8 = 6 remainder 2 = $6 14 = $6.25. The $2 left over is 25¢ each, not 20¢.

items.q: Raju’s rope is 3 times as long as Arjun’s rope. The two ropes are 10 m long altogether. How long is Arjun’s rope?
items.e: 4 units = 10 m, so 1 unit = 10 ÷ 4 = 104 m = 2 12 m. Arjun has 1 unit. 3 13 m is 10 ÷ 3: the model has 4 units, not 3.

items.q: Mrs Ng bought 5 kg of sugar. She used 1 kg and packed the rest equally into 3 containers. How much sugar is in each container?
items.e: 5 kg − 1 kg = 4 kg. 3 units = 4 kg, so 1 unit = 4 ÷ 3 = 1 13 kg. 1 23 kg shares all 5 kg and forgets the 1 kg used.

items.q: Xin Yi and Mei Ling have 9 ℓ of water altogether. Xin Yi has 2 ℓ more than Mei Ling. How much water does Mei Ling have?
items.e: Take away the extra 2 ℓ: 9 − 2 = 7 ℓ. 2 units = 7 ℓ, so 1 unit = 7 ÷ 2 = 3 12 ℓ. 5 12 ℓ is Xin Yi’s share, and 4 12 ℓ forgets the extra 2 ℓ.

items.q: Each child gets 34 of a pizza. There are 12 children. How many pizzas are there?
items.e: Each child gets 3 quarters, so 12 children get 12 × 3 = 36 quarters. 36 ÷ 4 = 9 pizzas. Check: 9 ÷ 12 = 912 = 34.

items.q: Kavya pours 4 ℓ of juice equally into 5 jugs. She serves 2 jugs to her guests. How much juice is left in the other jugs?
items.e: 5 units = 4 ℓ, so 1 unit = 4 ÷ 5 = 0.8 ℓ. 3 jugs are left: 3 × 0.8 = 2.4 ℓ. 1.6 ℓ is the 2 jugs she served.

items.q: Mr Tan cuts a 10 m plank into 7 equal pieces. How long is each piece, correct to 2 decimal places?
items.e: 10 ÷ 7 = 1.428… m. The 3rd decimal place is 8, so round up: 1.43 m. 1.3 m writes the remainder 3 as a decimal.

items.q: Wei Ming cycles 5 km in 3 equal laps at East Coast Park. How long is one lap, correct to 2 decimal places?
items.e: 5 ÷ 3 = 1.666… km. The 3rd decimal place is 6, so round up: 1.67 km. 0.6 km is 3 ÷ 5.

items.q: Mrs Lim shares 4 cakes equally among 5 tables at a party. At each table, the cake is shared equally among 4 children. What fraction of a cake does each child get?
items.e: There are 5 × 4 = 20 children. 4 cakes shared among 20 children: 4 ÷ 20 = 420 = 15 of a cake. 45 is the share of one table, and 120 forgets that there are 4 cakes.
